title: No orderable part is chosen for inductors L11/L12, so the +/-12 V converter cannot be assembled as ordered.
what: The two 6.8 uH inductors L11 and L12 of the LT3582 boost/inverting converter carry Murata part number DFE201610E-6R8M=P2, which no distributor lists, so the JLC bill of materials (BOM) line has no part number and is marked 'PART TO CHOOSE'. The inductor's saturation current (Isat, the current at which its inductance falls sharply) must exceed the worst-case peak current: about 0.78 A in L12 and 0.48 A in L11. Both in-stock TDK candidates named in the record meet this: the record's 0.70 A and 0.87 A are TDK's 'rated current', the smaller of Isat and the heating current Itemp, not saturation figures. What remains is to pick one and check its land pattern and height.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12, bottom side, footprint FPGA_LDO_V30A:L_Murata_DFE201610P. L11 at (94.45, 140.55), pads /VIN_3V3 and /SW_P (boost). L12 at (103.85, 142.9), rotation -90, pads /SW_N and GND (inverting). U1 LT3582EUD-12#PBF pins 3/4 (/SW_N), 12 (/SW_P), 5 (/VIN_3V3).
evidence: inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/FPGA_LDO_A_V12_BOM_JLC.csv line 15: 'L11,L12', JLCPCB Part # empty, note 'PART TO CHOOSE'; parts_status.csv line 15 'no part chosen'; JLC_Remarks_paste.txt line 29 'to be confirmed'. LT3582 p.3: ILIMIT_N 490/600/720 mA, ILIMIT_P 285/350/430 mA; p.18: IPK = ILIMIT + VIN x TOS / L, TOS 125 ns (inverting), 100 ns (boost). L12: 720 + 3.3 x 125 / 6.8 = 781 mA (796 mA if L is 20 % low; 661 mA at the typical limit). L11: 430 + 3.3 x 100 / 6.8 = 479 mA. TDK data sheets (LCSC copies): VLS201610HBX-6R8M-1 (C307855) Isat 0.88 A, Itemp 0.70 A, 1.0 mm tall; VLS201612HBX-6R8M-1 (C501945) Isat 0.91 A, Itemp 0.87 A, 1.2 mm tall; Isat defined at a 30 % inductance drop. V12_record/START_HERE.md line 52 quotes 0.70 A and 0.87 A. Land pattern: TDK 0.5 x 1.6 mm pads, 1.0 mm gap; board (exports/ldo_a/pads.csv) 0.55 x 1.60 mm, 0.90 mm gap; both 2.0 mm overall. Schematic MPN fields differ: L11 'Isat >= 0.6 A', L12 'Isat >= 0.8 A'.
source: ADI LT3582/LT3582-5/LT3582-12 data sheet 3582512fb, Rev B, p.3 (switch current limits) and p.18 'Choosing Inductors', https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf (read from a saved copy; analog.com timed out). TDK VLS201610HBX-1 / VLS201612HBX-1 data sheets p.1-3 (LCSC copies for C307855 and C501945).
consequence: Until a part is chosen the order cannot proceed, or JLC flags the line and leaves L11/L12 unplaced, and the +/-12 V stimulation rails do not work. A substitute with Isat below about 0.8 A would saturate in L12 at the switch current limit.
suggested_action: Pick C307855 or C501945 for both L11 and L12 after checking its land pattern and its 1.0 or 1.2 mm height on the bottom side. Enter the MPN and LCSC number on both parts and regenerate the JLC BOM.
already_known: V12_record/START_HERE.md (Parts table) and V12_order/FPGA_LDO_A_V12_BOM_JLC.csv list the part as unchosen. Both reviewers agree it blocks ordering. The record does not say the 0.70 A option may be too small for L12; one reviewer says the record quotes Itemp as the current rating of C307855.

title: The L2 AGND plane is the return plane for many L1 digital lanes, so their edge currents flow in analog ground.
what: L2 is filled as the analog ground (AGND) plane and lies only 0.071 mm under L1, so for 216 of the 506 mm of L1 FPGA-to-ASIC lanes it carries their return current (the current that flows back under a signal trace in the nearest plane). These lanes are 1.5 V logic referenced to digital ground (GND), and AGND meets GND only at net tie NT1 (a deliberate copper join between two ground nets), so the return current must cross through NT1 or the small L2-L3 plane capacitance. The grounds of the LT3042 regulators that make REF_VCM, VDD_FE and REF_VDD land in the same plane, and 84 mm of the over-AGND lane length runs just north of them. The rest of the L1 lanes cross L2 voids and reference L3 GND, so they also change reference plane along their length.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12, L1 lanes over the L2 (In1.Cu) AGND fill. Band y 128.6-133.8 just north of bottom-side U8 (93.2, 135.6, REF_VCM), U2 (98.85, 135.6, VDD_FE) and U6 (104.5, 135.6, REF_VDD). Worst lanes: ASIC5_DATA5-8, READ, SYNC, CLK32MHz_Out and STIM_CHB_SHARED, 12.2-13.0 mm each over AGND, mostly at x 108-110, y 112.5-120.8, plus x 99-104, y 112-114 near J3/J4. AGND vias e.g. (101.95, 134.75) for R201/C203 and (99.50, 138.57). NT1 at (100.58, 121.0) on L6.
evidence: pcbnew sampling of L1 tracks against the filled L2 AGND polygon on a copy of the board (scratch/verify-ldo_a-f2-files/ov.py, bb.py): 506.0 mm of L1 digital lanes on 51 nets; 215.8 mm on 41 nets over AGND; 84.3 mm of that in y 128.6-133.8. A second run at 0.05 mm steps: 511.4 mm total, 215.4 mm over AGND, 282.4 mm over L2 voids with L3 GND below. board.json: L2 carries 79 track nets, 465.9 mm; without GND and ASIC_DVDD, 77 nets and 445.4 mm, of which 45 nets over 2 mm carry 421 mm and the rest are short via jogs. Only ASIC1/2/3/4/6 CLK32MHz_Out are on L2 (ASIC2 a 0.6 mm stub). zones.csv: AGND on L2 546 mm2 of an 832 mm2 board. stackup.txt: L1-L2 0.071 mm, L2-L3 0.201 mm, er 4.46. C = 8.854e-12 x 4.46 x 546e-6 / 0.201e-3 = 107 pF, about 15 ohm at 100 MHz. pads.csv: J1/J2 have no AGND pins (GND on 14/15/27/34/41/50/66); on the ASIC board J3/J4 pins 42/44 are AGND and 46/48 DGND, and no part joins them except the ASIC dies. NT1 is the only AGND-GND tie on Option A. Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: LVCMOS15. parts_review_V21 states NT1 keeps digital return current out of AGND; the layout does not do that.
source: Engineering judgement (mixed-signal grounding: high-frequency return current flows in the nearest plane, and an analog reference plane should not carry digital return current). Related: ADI LT3042 data sheet 3042fa, Rev A, p.12 (SET pin, RSET ground Kelvin-connected to the load) and p.15 (CSET and output-capacitor grounds), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf (read from a saved copy).
consequence: Edge currents from the 32 MHz-class lanes of eight ASICs move AGND relative to GND beside the reference regulators and at the port, and the ASIC sees that noise between its AGND and DGND pads. Expect spurs on REF_VCM, REF_VDD, VDD_FE and AGND in a microvolt recording system; the size is unknown and nothing is measured.
suggested_action: Decide before ordering: either make the lanes reference GND (GND on L2 under the lane corridors, AGND kept as islands under the LDO cells tied at NT1), or keep the layout and plan a bring-up measurement of noise on REF_VCM and AGND while the lanes toggle.
already_known: V11_record/START_HERE.md lists only 'DVDD track on the AGND plane layer (L2) is now 15 mm' as open, which understates the problem.

title: Two stacked copies of the only ASIC board on file would short data outputs and leave ASIC3/4/7/8 unconnected.
what: On the ASIC board every J3 pin is wired to the J4 pin with the same number, so a board stacked on it sees the same nets. Its two chips drive DATA1-8, CLK32MHZ, SYNC and READ (all ASIC outputs) on odd pins only; the 22 even-pin T_ lines are pass-through lines that touch only J3 and J4. Option A puts the near board's chips on the odd pins and the far board's chips (ASIC3/4 and ASIC7/8) on the even pins, so it works only with a separate far ('Top') variant whose chips use the even T_ pins. That variant's CAD is not in the workspace, so its pin map cannot be checked against Option A.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12: J4 even pins 10-22, 26-32 and 60-80 (ASIC3/ASIC4) and the same J3 pins (ASIC7/ASIC8); pins 3 and 5 open on J3 and J4. ASIC board: J3 (bottom, DF40C-80DS) and J4 (top, DF40C-80DP), both at (135.54, 71.0), all 80 pins; U01_BCD1, U01_BCD2.
evidence: exports/asic/connectors.csv: J3.n and J4.n carry the same net for n = 1..80 apart from the unconnected spares 2/4/6/8/24/58; both at rotation 180 with pin 1 at the same XY. exports/asic/pads.csv: /D<8> reaches J3.37, J4.37 and U01_BCD1.DATAR<1>; /T_D<8> reaches only J3.62 and J4.62; all 22 T_ nets have 2 pads; /DISC_OUT on pin 5 (BCD1), /DISC_OUT(2) on pin 3 (BCD2). exports/asic/drc.json: 0 unconnected. exports/ldo_a/connectors.csv: J4.37 = ASIC1_DATA8, J4.62 = ASIC3_DATA8, J3.62 = ASIC7_DATA8. Pin-by-pin comparison under near-odd / far-even (scratch/verify-ldo_a-f3-files/chk.py): 88 lane pins, 0 mismatches. ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 43 and rows 111-117: DATA, CLK32MHZ, SYNC and READ are outputs to the FPGA. boards/asic holds one PCB.kicad_pcb; Board-1024.zip holds only backups of it. sandwich_hub_options/START_HERE.md line 29: the 'Top' file is still needed.
source: ASIC board PCB.kicad_pcb (exports/asic/connectors.csv, pads.csv); the ASIC designer's J3 pinout spreadsheet (inputs/asic/J3_pinout__J3_Pinout.csv); ASIC reference ASIC_REFERENCE.md signal map; schematic V30A port note 'Unverified: far-board wiring'. Engineering judgement: two push-pull outputs must not share one line.
consequence: Two copies of the existing board on one port would put two output drivers on each odd data line (corrupting ASIC1/2/5/6 data too), tie the DISC_OUT outputs on pins 3 and 5 together, and leave four of the eight ASICs connected to nothing. If the far variant's pins differ from Option A's even-pin map, a board spin follows.
suggested_action: Before ordering, obtain (or have drawn) the far-board 'Top' ASIC board with its chips on the even T_ pins and DISC_OUT off pins 3/5, then run the same pin-by-pin check against Option A J3/J4.
already_known: parts_review_V21/index.html ('second ASIC board ... must be the top variant'); schematic V30A port note. The reviewer agrees with major.

title: Option A has four SPI data pairs for eight ASICs, so each near/far ASIC pair gets identical configuration.
what: Each ASIC is set up over SPI (a serial configuration bus); its data inputs SPI_DINL/SPI_DINR carry its gains, DAC settings and stimulus tables. Option A routes only four pairs (STIM_CHIP1..4) to pins 57/59 and 23/25 of each port, and the ASIC board buses those pins straight through to the stacked board with no separate pass-through copy, so ASIC1/3, 2/4, 5/7 and 6/8 receive identical data. The ASIC designer's Pins sheet lists SPI_DL/SPI_DR as per-chip inputs. SPI_CLK (per port), SPI_LATCH and the stimulation controls are also shared, so a far board cannot be set to record only.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12: STIM_CHIP1 DR/DL J2.44/46 to J4.57/59; STIM_CHIP2 J1.59/57 to J4.23/25; STIM_CHIP3 J2.19/17 to J3.57/59; STIM_CHIP4 J1.20/22 to J3.23/25. BOARD1_SPI_CLK on J4.63, BOARD3_SPI_CLK on J3.63. ASIC board J3/J4 pins 57/59 (U01_BCD1) and 23/25 (U01_BCD2).
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml: 8 STIM_CHIPn_SPI_DL/DR nets, 2 nodes each. exports/asic/connectors.csv: J3.n = J4.n; pins 57/59 are /SPI_DINR and /SPI_DINL, 23/25 are /SPI_DINR(2) and /SPI_DINL(2), with no T_ copies. inputs/asic/Pins__Sheet1.csv: SPI_DL and SPI_DR under 'Not Shared / Chip in'; SPI_CLK, SPI_LATCH, CLKH and STIM controls under 'Shared'. ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 4: the SPI stream carries DR_DAC, AR_DAC, Gain_Right, Gain_Left and the L/R stimulus tables. Spares: Option A J1 has 13 unconnected contacts (29-33, 35-37, 39, 43, 45, 47, 49); the Frontend's J1 has the same pins unconnected; ASIC board pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 are separate unconnected nets on J3 and J4. Frontend V43 schematic note: NONSTIM SPI and BOARD2/4 clock nets removed, identical configuration of stacked boards listed as unverified. Schematic V30A port note: 'recording-only boards sharing stim-chip SPI data' unverified.
source: ASIC designer's Pins sheet (inputs/asic/Pins__Sheet1.csv); ASIC reference ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 4; schematic V30A port note.
consequence: The two chips in the same position on a stacked pair cannot be configured or stimulated independently. Reversing this after ordering means respinning both Option A and the Frontend.
suggested_action: Get the ASIC designer's decision before ordering. If per-chip SPI is needed, add four pairs through the J1 spares on both the Frontend (FPGA pins and firmware) and Option A, to ASIC pins 2/4/6/8 or 24/58, with matching wiring on the far variant and pass-through on the near board.
already_known: Schematic V30A port note; also raised in the system reviews. The reviewer agrees with major.

title: The 14 Frontend GND pins on J1/J2 reach the ground planes only through thin L1 traces and three laser vias.
what: J1 and J2 each have 7 GND pins spread over y 122.6-133.0. On this board each connector's GND pins are joined only by a 0.2 mm, 10.4 mm L1 trace, which drops to the L3/L4 GND planes through a 0.10 mm laser via (a small via through one thin layer) and a buried via: one such pair for J2, two for J1. These few vias carry the return current of about 108 signals on J1/J2 and the supply return of VIN_3V3 on J2.68-70. The trace adds roughly 2.5-7 nH of return inductance shared by up to 7 pins, which gives away most of the benefit of having 7 ground pins.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/board.json: of 27 GND vias only 3 span L1-L2, at (108.75, 133.0), (91.25, 133.0) and (89.9, 129.8); zones.csv: no GND pour on L1 or L2. Copper path search (scratch/ldo_a-layout/conn.py, re-run in scratch/verify-ldo_a-f5-engineering/chk.py): J2.14 to L3 67 squares, J2.66 15, J1.50 29.3. Removing via (108.75, 133.00) cuts J2.14 and J2.66 off from L3 on this board. J3/J4 GND pins 46/48 each have an in-pad through via. L2 AGND fill is present at only 5 of 28 samples under the traces, so they mostly reference L3 about 0.30 mm below: about 0.5 nH/mm, 4-5 nH over 10.4 mm (2.5-7.7 nH across reference assumptions). Pin map J1_J2_pin_map_V5.csv: about 108 signal pins, 14 GND. Rough bounce: 16 edges of about 7.5 mA in 2 ns through 4 nH is about 0.24 V (not simulated; ASIC drive strength unknown). Supply current is small (about 11.6 mA core per ASIC board, J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv). Under J2, L2 between y 122.6 and 129.8 has no signal tracks.
source: Engineering judgement (return-path continuity at board-to-board connectors).
consequence: Ground bounce and crosstalk between the ASIC data, clock and SPI lanes when many switch together, possibly a few tenths of a volt against 1.5 V logic margins; not simulated. On this board J2 depends on one laser via; if it fails, J2's ground returns must detour through the Frontend and J1.
suggested_action: Add a laser plus buried via (or a through via) in or beside each J1/J2 GND pad, as J3/J4 already have; L3/L4 are solid under the pads and L2 is free at y 122.6-129.8. Re-run DRC.

title: LT3582 VIN pin 5 has no local input capacitor; it is fed through two microvias and 8.6 mm of 0.3 mm L5 trace.
what: The LT3582 data sheet requires VIN to be bypassed locally with a ceramic capacitor, and its layout figure places the input capacitor right at pin 5. On V12, U1 pin 5 sits on a separate 2.36 mm2 L6 copper island holding only the pin and one microvia (a small laser-drilled via between adjacent layers); its only feed is 8.61 mm of 0.30 mm L5 trace to a second microvia under C1 (22 uF), 8.35 mm away. C11, the 4.7 uF part the schematic names as the converter's input capacitor, sits on the main VIN pour and reaches the pin only through the same trace. The inverting channel's pulsed switch current therefore flows in a loop (input capacitor, VIN, SWN, D12, C21, ground) about 8 x 4 mm instead of a few millimetres.
evidence: pcbnew on a copy of the board (scratch/verify-ldo_a-f6-files/chk.py, isl2.py; scratch/verify-ldo_a-f6-engineering/chk.py): the L6 /VIN_3V3 pour has two pieces, 113.21 mm2 and 2.36 mm2; the small piece holds only U1.5 and via (100.75, 144.85). L5 trace 1.414 + 7.2 = 8.61 mm at 0.30 mm; both vias drill 0.10 mm, pad 0.26 mm. Distances from U1.5 (exports/ldo_a/pads.csv): C1.1 8.35 mm, C11.1 4.43 mm, C2.1 9.71 mm. Loop bounding box about 8.2 x 4.0 mm. Schematic note: 'Changed from Figure 13: ... C1 -> C11 4.7 uF 10 V 0603'. Estimate: 0.3 mm trace between L4 GND (0.201 mm) and L6 (0.071 mm) is about 0.2-0.35 nH/mm, so 2-3 nH for the feed and 3-5 nH for the loop. At the 490-720 mA inverting current limit (p.3, reached at start-up) this gives a few tenths of a volt of spike at VIN; at the 10 mA design load peaks are much lower (p.10). No project record (V11_record, V12_record, V12_checks, parts_review_V21) lists this.
source: ADI LT3582/LT3582-5/LT3582-12 data sheet 3582512fb, Rev B, p.8 (Pin 5 VIN, local ceramic bypass), p.19 (Capacitor Selection, 4.7 uF input), p.21 (Board Layout Considerations, Figure 12), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf (read from a saved text copy; analog.com timed out).
consequence: Switching noise and ringing on VIN_3V3, which also feeds the seven regulators U2-U8 beside the low-noise LT3042 rows, and possibly erratic switching. This is plausible but not shown; only a measurement after build would show its size.
suggested_action: Move C11 (or add a 1-4.7 uF ceramic plus 100 nF) directly at U1 pin 5 on the island, with a short ground via, and check the placement against data sheet Figure 12.

title: U1 LT3582EUD-12#PBF is out of stock at JLC, and the order files do not forbid a non -12 substitute.
what: U1 is the boost/inverting converter that makes the +/-12 V stimulation supply. JLC shows 0 in stock and 0 orderable, so it needs Global Sourcing or a pre-order. On this board U1's I2C pins CA, SDA and SCL are tied to GND and VPP (the pin used to program its OTP, one-time-programmable, memory) is left open, so the chip can never be configured on the board. Only the -12 version, which leaves the factory set to +/-12 V, works here: a plain LT3582 ships with blank OTP that keeps both outputs off, and an LT3582-5 gives only +/-5 V, too little for the +/-10 V LDOs. The schematic states that the -12 version is needed, but the JLC remark, BOM and START_HERE parts table do not forbid a substitute.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12, U1 LT3582EUD-12#PBF, bottom side at (100.0, 142.6), rotation 180. Pin 1 CA, pin 15 SDA, pin 16 SCL and EP 17 on GND; pin 14 VPP unconnected; pin 9 on STIM_POS_12V, pin 2 on STIM_NEG_12V, pin 8 SHDN on EN_ASIC_RAILS.
evidence: inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/parts_status.csv row C670975: 5 needed, JLC stock 0, orderable 0, read 2026-11-10 16:04. LCSC public product data today: C670975 stock 0 and the #TRPBF listing C670976 stock 0 (one checker; the other found no stock figure on the product page). inputs/ldo_a/V12_record/START_HERE.md line 50 records both at 0. exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml and pads.csv: U1 pins 1, 15, 16 and 17 on GND, pin 14 unconnected-(U1-VPP-Pad14). FPGA_LDO_A_V12_BOM_JLC.csv line 20 and JLC_Remarks_paste.txt line 28 list the stock gap with no variant restriction. The schematic text reads 'I2C/OTP unused on the -12 version'. The DigiKey lead time in the original report was not verified.
source: ADI LT3582/LT3582-5/LT3582-12 data sheet 3582512fb, Rev B: p.8 pin functions (VPP floats unless programming; SDA/SCL may be tied to GND), p.11 (CA/SDA/SCL grounded when I2C is unused), p.12 'LT3582-5/LT3582-12 Chip Configuration' and 'Registers and OTP' (base part ships with all-zero OTP), p.13 register table (PUSEQ 00 = outputs disabled). https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf (read from the project's copy, SHA-256 af3660d7...; analog.com timed out).
consequence: Assembly waits on U1. If a base LT3582 is fitted the board makes no +/-12 V and cannot be fixed over I2C; an -5 part gives +/-5 V. The board can still be brought up without U1 by cutting JP1/JP2 and feeding +/-V from a bench supply at TP8/TP9, which is awkward on a head stack.
suggested_action: Get a quoted lead time for LT3582EUD-12#PBF or #TRPBF before ordering, and add one line to the assembly remark and the START_HERE parts table that only the -12 suffix is acceptable.
already_known: V12_record/START_HERE.md lists the stock gap; the reviewer agrees. The variant restriction is not recorded.

title: ASIC_VDD10 has no clamp diode to AGND, so a power-down can pull the LT3042 output below its -0.3 V limit.
what: The ASIC's stimulator sits between ASIC_VDD10 (+10 V from U9, an LT3042) and ASIC_VSS10 (-10 V from U10, an LT3094). After power is lost, ASIC current flowing only between the two rails drags them toward each other, while other paths drain each rail to ground at different rates, so one rail can cross 0 V. Where the rails end depends on the ASIC's current split and the regulators' shutdown currents, none of which is documented; in about two thirds of the modelled cases VDD10 goes below -0.3 V, the LT3042's absolute maximum, and an internal substrate diode (an unintended junction inside the chip) carries the current. In the other cases VSS10 ends up to about 2.5 V above AGND, which the LT3094 tolerates but for which the ASIC has no recorded tolerance.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12: U9 LT3042 OUT/OUTS pins 10/9 on ASIC_VDD10 with C902 (22 uF 1206, bottom, 94.925, 122.95); U10 LT3094 OUT/OUTS pins 10-12 on ASIC_VSS10 with C1002 (22 uF 1206, 106.75, 122.95) and C1004 (10 uF 0805, 103.45, 122.85); J3/J4 pin 36 (VDD10) and pin 54 (VSS10) to the ASIC boards.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/nets.csv: ASIC_VDD10 = C902.1, J3.36, J4.36, U9.9, U9.10; ASIC_VSS10 = C1002.1, C1004.1, J3.54, J4.54, U10.10-12; no diode, resistor or test point to AGND on either. D11/D12 are LT3582 converter diodes, not rail clamps. With only a load between the rails, the end voltage is 10 V x (Cp - Cn)/(Cp + Cn): -1.85 V with nominal 22/32 uF, about -1.6 V with typical derating. Ground-referenced drains shift this: LT3042 overshoot-recovery sink up to 15 mA (LT3042 p.21), LT3094 ground current, and the LT3582-12 VOUTN power-down discharge of 1.4/2.8/4.2 mA (3582512fb p.3), reaching VSS10 through the LT3094 OUT-to-IN diode. A sensitivity model with these drains (scratch/verify-ldo_a-g1-engineering/m.py; Cp 12-22 uF, Cn 30-64 uF, bridge current 0.1-8 mA, ground sinks 0-15 mA) has VDD10 crossing -0.3 V in about two thirds of cases and VSS10 ending +0.07 to +2.5 V in the rest. inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv gives VDD10/VSS10 a 2 mA maximum each per ASIC board, so the original 23 mA load case is above budget. The ASIC boards add C18/C19 and C25/C26 (0201, no value given).
source: ADI LT3042 data sheet Rev A (3042fa): p.2 Absolute Maximum Ratings (OUT, OUTS -0.3 V), p.5 Note 10 (do not drive OUT/OUTS more than 0.3 V below GND, including during faults), p.14 pin functions, p.21 Protection Features. https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf . ADI LT3094 data sheet Rev 0: p.28 Protection Features (OUT may be pulled up to 20 V above GND, 25 mA, without damage). https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3094.pdf . Neither data sheet shows a split-supply clamp; the need follows from the LT3042 rating. Read from local copies; analog.com timed out.
consequence: On some power-downs the LT3042 output pin goes past its absolute maximum and its substrate diode carries a few mA; damage is unlikely but outside the data sheet. Where VSS10 ends positive instead, the ASIC's negative stimulator rail sits above AGND with no recorded tolerance.
suggested_action: Add a Schottky from AGND (anode) to ASIC_VDD10 (cathode) beside C902, and optionally one from ASIC_VSS10 (anode) to AGND (cathode) beside C1002, rated VR of at least 20 V with VF under 0.3 V at 10-25 mA. Confirm with a scope on the first board, powering down with and without ASIC boards.

title: On a light-load power-down, U10 (LT3094) output falls over 0.3 V below its input, past its absolute maximum.
what: The LT3094 must never have OUT, OUTS or SET more than 0.3 V below IN, even in a fault. When 3.3 V is lost the LT3582 stops, but C3 holds EN_ASIC_RAILS up, so U10 stays on for about 49 ms (about 30-35 ms if C3 loses capacitance at 3.3 V bias). U10's own 2-4 mA ground current flows into its input node and raises it toward 0 V, while ASIC_VSS10 moves only with the ASIC load; with little or no load, including no ASIC boards fitted, the input passes the output and an internal substrate diode conducts. Pulling EN_ASIC_RAILS low with 3.3 V present (TP4 today) does the same for about 200 ms, because the LT3582-12 power-down discharge pulls U10's input toward ground while U10 is off.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12: U10 LT3094 (IN pins 1, 2, 13 and PGFB pin 5 on STIM_PRE_NEG; OUT pins 11/12 and OUTS pin 10 on ASIC_VSS10; SET pin 8 with C1003 1 uF and R1001 100k); input C1001 (10 uF, 107.725, 129.71) plus C21 (22 uF) through bridged JP2; output C1002 (22 uF) and C1004 (10 uF); EN_ASIC_RAILS (R1 10k, C3 4.7 uF, TP4, U1 pin 8 SHDN, U10 pin 3).

JP2 is 'Bridged' with real copper in the .kicad_pcb, so input and output are both 32 uF nominal; no diode or bleeder joins the two nets. Enable hold: R1 10k with the LT3582's 222k SHDN pull-down and C3 4.7 uF gives 45 ms x ln(3.16/1.06) = 49 ms nominal. To keep OUT above IN the ASIC must draw more than I_GND x Cout/Cin, about 2.4-4 mA at nominal capacitance and more with derating. Models (original shutdown2.py; scratch/verify-ldo_a-g2-files/sim.py; a hand calculation): at 0-0.5 mA load OUT goes more than 0.5 V below IN in every case, starting about 6-34 ms after power loss, lasting about 15-40 ms, with about 0.5-2.6 mA in the diode; at 2 mA load in 4 of 6 cases. Controlled shutdown (PDDIS = 1 on the -12 version): about 1.4 mA for about 190 ms at typical values, range 0.7-2.1 mA for 130-390 ms. In this case SET stays above IN because R1001 drains C1003.
source: ADI LT3094 data sheet Rev 0: p.3 Absolute Maximum Ratings (OUT, OUTS, SET with respect to IN, -0.3 V), p.4 GND pin current (2.35 mA typ, 4 mA max), p.6 Note 2, Note 11 (ground current measured in dropout), p.15 pin functions (EN/UV threshold; OUT/OUTS substrate diode). https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3094.pdf . ADI LT3582 data sheet 3582512fb Rev B: p.3 VOUTN power-down discharge, p.8 SHDN pull-down, p.12 LT3582-12 defaults, p.16 Power-Down Discharge. https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf . Read from local copies; analog.com timed out.
consequence: Every unloaded power cycle forward-biases a substrate junction in U10 at about 1-2 mA for tens of milliseconds, and every TP4 shutdown does so for about 200 ms. Damage is not certain, but reliability and latch-up behaviour are unspecified, and the exposure grows if an FPGA-driven enable is added later.

title: LT3582 ripple crossing the single tie NT1 puts about 0.4-1.3 mV rms between the ASIC's AGND and DGND pins.
what: The capacitors that share VIN_3V3 and the +/-12 V outputs with the LT3582 converter return to AGND, so part of the converter's pulsed current flows into AGND and back to GND through NT1, the only AGND-GND tie (a net tie is a copper bridge that joins two nets at one chosen point). The ASIC board keeps AGND and DGND separate, and its AGND pins (J4.42/44) and DGND pins (J4.46/48) sit at the two ends of the NT1 chain, so the whole tie voltage appears between the ASIC's two grounds. The original report counted the chain as one 54-square trace; each side actually has two parallel 0.2 mm traces, so the chain is about 28-29 squares (14-16 mOhm) and the voltage is about a quarter lower than first stated. How much of it reaches the recordings depends on the ASIC's ground rejection, which is not documented.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12, bottom layer L6: NT1 (pads at x 100.08 and 101.08, y 121.0). AGND side: traces from the J4.42 via (99.983, 114.8) and the J4.44 via (100.383, 115.1) to NT1.2. GND side: traces from the J4.46 via (100.783, 114.8) and the J4.48 via (101.183, 115.1) to NT1.1. AGND-returned C201, C601, C801 (10 uF) and C401, C501, C701 (1 uF) on VIN_3V3; C901 and C1001 (10 uF) through bridged JP1/JP2. L11.1 at (93.725, 140.55).
evidence: exports/ldo_a/board.json: four 0.2 mm L6 traces, J4.42 path 29.9 squares, J4.44 path 28.7, J4.46 path 30.2, J4.48 path 28.5; a pcbnew fill check on a scratch copy puts both AGND vias in the L2 plane and both GND vias in the L3/L4 planes. The parallel pairs give about 28-29 squares, 14.4 mOhm at 0.49 mOhm/square (B.Cu 0.035 mm, stackup.txt), about 14.6-16 mOhm with the tie, against 27.5 mOhm in the original. Nearest capacitors to L11.1: C701 (AGND) 3.34 mm, C801 (AGND) 8.21 mm, C11 (GND) 9.40 mm, C1 (GND) 16.04 mm. exports/asic/netlist.xml: /AGND on J3/J4.42/44, /DGND on J3/J4.46/48, no tie on the ASIC board. Rerun of the original lumped model with 14.6 mOhm (scratch/verify-ldo_a-g4-engineering/fix): NT1 current about 22/52/72 mA rms and AGND-DGND about 0.4/0.9/1.3 mV rms below 2 MHz at 2/10/25 mA per output, against 0.53/1.23/1.74 mV in the original; full-band switch-edge peaks about 6-29 mV p-p, set mainly by the assumed 4 nH loop. Capacitor derating and the 4 nH are model assumptions. An ASIC on J3 (L1) sees about 1-2 mOhm of via barrel added.
source: Engineering judgement (return-path analysis for split grounds). ADI LT3582 data sheet 3582512fb Rev B: p.6-7 switching frequency and waveforms, p.8 VIN pin function, p.10 Operation, p.22 Figure 13. https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf (read from the project's copy; analog.com timed out).
consequence: Roughly 0.4-1.3 mV rms at the converter's switching frequencies sits between the ASIC's analog and digital grounds whenever the stimulation converter runs. Whether it shows in the recordings depends on the ASIC's unknown ground and supply rejection.
suggested_action: Before ordering, decide how to keep converter ripple off AGND: feed U1/L11 through a small ferrite with their own GND-returned input capacitors, or return the converter-side capacitors to GND after checking the LT3042 input-capacitor grounding advice. Otherwise measure J4.44 to J4.46 at bring-up with stimulation running.

title: U3, U4 and U5 regulate against a different ground point from the ASIC's, so NT1 ripple lands on three rails.
what: A regulator holds its output steady relative to its own ground pin, so if the load is decoupled to a different ground, any voltage between the two grounds appears on the rail at the load. U3 (VDD_ADC) is on GND, but the ASIC board decouples VDD_ADC to AGND; U5 (DVDD) is on AGND, but the ASIC board decouples DVDD to DGND; U4 (VDD_DRIVER) and its capacitors sit on an L6 AGND island that reaches the L2 plane only through NT1.2, about halfway along the NT1 tie. The NT1 ripple from the LT3582 therefore appears on these rails at the ASIC, hundreds of times above the ripple the TPS7A20 regulators pass from VIN_3V3. The effect on recordings is not established, because the ASIC's supply rejection on these rails is not documented; DVDD is a digital rail, where about 1 mV rms is harmless.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12: U3 pins 2/5 and C301/C302 on GND (VDD_ADC to J3/J4.56); U5 pins 2/5, C501, C502 and C54 on AGND (DVDD to J3/J4.34); U4 pins 2/5, C401, C402 and C53 (VDD_DRIVER to J3/J4.38) on an L6 AGND island with C51 (VDD_FE), C55 (REF_VDD) and C57 (REF_VCM), joined to L2 only through NT1.2 and the traces to the J4.42/J4.44 vias.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml: U3.2/.5, C301.2, C302.2 on GND; U4/U5 grounds and C401/C402/C501/C502/C53/C54/C57 on AGND; VDD_ADC has only C302 on this board (no C52). exports/asic/netlist.xml: VDD_ADC capacitors C1, C34-C38 and VDD_DRIVER capacitors C3, C39-C43 to /AGND; DVDD capacitors C7-C14 to /DGND; no AGND-DGND part. exports/asic/parts.csv: only 2 of 6, 2 of 8 and 2 of 6 of these 0201 capacitors are placed, none with a value. Nodal solve of the L6 copper (scratch/verify-ldo_a-g6-files/res2.py): tie 14.6 mOhm pad to pad, NT1.2 to L2 8.5 mOhm, U4.5 to L2 20.0 mOhm, against 27.5 and 13.4 mOhm in the original. Rerun of the original ripple model with 14.6 mOhm: VDD_ADC and DVDD about 0.4/1.0/1.3-1.6 mV rms and VDD_DRIVER about 0.2/0.5/0.7 mV rms (50 kHz-2 MHz, at 2/10/25 mA per +/-12 V output), against uV-level VIN ripple after the TPS7A20. inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv gives VDD10/VSS10 a 2 mA maximum each; with about 2 mA of LDO quiescent current the realistic load is 2-5 mA per output, so the 2 mA column applies. inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md lists 'VDD_ADC ground' as still open. ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 7 shows the crossed ground assignment was inherited.
source: TI TPS7A20 data sheet SBVS338H (July 2024): electrical table PSRR rows (75 dB at 100 kHz, 45 dB at 1 MHz, 20 mA) and note (3), voltages with respect to the GND pin. https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf (one checker could not re-extract the PSRR rows; the conclusion does not depend on them). Engineering judgement for the ground-reference analysis.
consequence: The ADC and driver supplies carry roughly 0.2-1 mV rms of converter ripple at realistic loads, which may fold into the recording band. Its effect in ADC codes cannot be stated without the ASIC designer's supply-rejection figures.
suggested_action: Before ordering, put U3 and its capacitors on AGND, put U5 and its capacitors on GND (the ASIC's DGND), and give U4 and its capacitors their own via to the L2 AGND plane instead of the NT1.2 trace.
already_known: Already reported as minor: 'The DVDD and VDD_ADC regulators return to the opposite ground from the one the ASIC board decouples those rails to' (ldo_a-regulators, ldo_a-connectivity). title: LDO input capacitors return to AGND, so some LT3582 ripple crosses NT1, which is not where the schematic says.
what: The LT3582's own capacitors return to GND, but the LDO input capacitors on the same supply nets return to AGND, so part of the converter ripple current enters AGND and must leave through NT1, the single AGND-GND tie. That share is set by path impedance rather than by capacitance and is probably well below half: a lumped estimate gives about 30% at 50-300 kHz and about 11% at 1 MHz. The schematic's VIN_3V3 ENTRY note asks for NT1 beside U9/U10, but NT1 sits about 6 mm from the J3/J4 AGND pins, between the regulators and the connector; moving it would not by itself change the AGND-GND voltage at the ASIC connector, which depends on the tie impedance. The input-capacitor grounds follow the LT3042 data sheet, which asks for the input capacitor ground to sit close to the output capacitor ground, so simply moving them to GND conflicts with it.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12: AGND-returned C201, C601, C801 (10 uF) and C401, C501, C701 (1 uF) on VIN_3V3; C901 (95.45, 129.71) on STIM_PRE_POS and C1001 (107.725, 129.71) on STIM_PRE_NEG, reached through bridged JP1/JP2. GND-returned C1, C2, C11, C301 on VIN_3V3 and C14, C15, C21 on the converter outputs. NT1 on L6 at (100.58, 121.0); U9 (95.4, 126.34), U10 (107.55, 126.34), U1 (100.0, 142.6).
evidence: exports/ldo_a/pads.csv and nets.csv: AGND pads include C201.2, C401.2, C501.2, C601.2, C701.2, C801.2, C901.2, C1001.2; GND pads include C1.2, C2.2, C11.2, C14.2, C15.2, C21.2, C301.2. NT1 is the only part with both AGND and GND pads. Nominal VIN_3V3 capacitance is 33 uF on AGND and 27.8 uF on GND, but C11 (4.7 uF) is 4 mm and C1 (22 uF) about 8 mm from U1 with direct GND vias. board.json: NT1.2 is fed by L6 traces from the J4.42 and J4.44 vias and from the C55/C57 AGND pads; NT1.1 by traces from the J4.46 and J4.48 vias. Distances from NT1: U9 7.44 mm, U10 8.78 mm, C901 10.1 mm, C1001 11.27 mm, J4.42 5.97 mm. boards/ldo_a/FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_sch line 1069: 'place NT1 beside U9/U10', bond location listed as unverified. inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md: V8 placed NT1 beside U9/U10; a later re-placement moved it under the J4 rail pins. inputs/ldo_a/parts_review_V21/index.html line 58 records the C901/C1001 crossing; START_HERE.md in that folder does not. exports/frontend: VIN_3V3 feeds MPM3833C U2/U3/U4/U13 pins 13/14, which have their own input capacitors on the Frontend, so their ripple share here is small.
source: Engineering judgement (split-ground return paths). Schematic V30A, VIN_3V3 ENTRY note. ADI LT3042 data sheet Rev A: p.15-16 (tie the input capacitor ground close to the output capacitor ground; 0.1-0.5 Ohm series input resistance damps the input), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf . ADI LT3582 data sheet 3582512fb Rev B: p.8 VIN bypass, p.10 Operation (frequency varies with load), p.19 input capacitor, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf .

suggested_action: Decide before ordering whether to lower the tie impedance (plane vias directly at NT1 with short, wide copper) or add a small series resistor or ferrite between the converter's VIN node and the LDO input branch; otherwise measure AGND-to-GND ripple at NT1 and at J3/J4 pins 42/44 on the first board with stimulation running.

title: The +/-10 V stimulation rails can reach +/-10.3 V, with no ASIC or capacitor rating to show that is safe.
what: R901 and R1001 (100k, 1%) set the stimulation rails ASIC_VDD10 and ASIC_VSS10 to +10.0 V and -10.0 V. The regulator output equals its SET pin current times the SET resistor, and that current varies from 98 to 102 uA over temperature, so the rails can span about 9.70 to 10.30 V in size. The only requirement on file is the ASIC designer's pin sheet, which gives +/-10 V with no maximum or tolerance; the ASIC reference says the chip's '+/-10 V' figure is stimulator output range, not a supply rating. The files cannot settle whether 10.3 V is within the rating of the ASIC and of the four 0201 capacitors on these rails on the ASIC board; a written answer from the ASIC designer would.
where: FPGA-LDO A: U9/R901 (/ASIC_VDD10) and U10/R1001 (/ASIC_VSS10); J3/J4 pin 36 (VDD10) and pin 54 (VSS10). ASIC board: C18, C19 on /VDD10 and C25, C26 on /VSS10, 0201 size.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml: R901 100k 1% from Net-(U9-SET) to AGND; R1001 100k 1% from Net-(U10-SET) to AGND. Worst case 102 uA x 101 kOhm = 10.30 V; 98 uA x 99 kOhm = 9.70 V. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_Nine_Rail_Design_Intent.csv: inherited LDO Board A U8 /VDD10 RSET 90000 -> 9.0 V (supplier BOM 91000 -> 9.1 V), approved voltage window UNKNOWN. ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 7: the +/-10 V figure is stimulation-output compliance; open item U02. J3_pinout__Power_Pins.csv: VDD10 10 V, VSS10 -10 V. exports/asic/pads.csv: only C18, C19, C25 and C26 are placed on these rails (C15-C17 and C20-C24 exist only in the schematic); exports/asic/parts.csv gives value 'C_Small_US' with no voltage or MPN field.
source: ADI LT3042 data sheet Rev A, p.3, and LT3094 data sheet Rev 0, p.4 (SET current 98-102 uA over temperature); ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 7 and open item U02.
consequence: If the ASIC's high-voltage devices or the 0201 capacitors are rated at 10 V, every ASIC could sit at or above its rating, with no way to trim the rails on the board.
suggested_action: Get the ASIC designer's written VDD10/VSS10 maximum and the voltage rating of the ASIC board's 0201 rail capacitors. If either is 10 V, change R901/R1001 to 93.1k-95.3k (about 9.3-9.5 V).
already_known: parts_review_V21 START_HERE.md S3 (resolved in V23 by following the designer's +/-10 V sheet); the schematic note asks to confirm the ASIC board 0201 rating (>= 16 V). The reviewer agrees the confirmation is still open and minor.

title: The 0.75 V REF_VCM regulator U8 has no minimum load, which the LT3042 needs for stability below 1 V.
what: U8 (LT3042) makes the 0.75 V common-mode reference ASIC_REF_VCM, and below 1 V output the LT3042 needs at least 10 uA of load to stay stable. Nothing on this board or the ASIC board loads the net with a resistor; the ASIC board puts only capacitors and ASIC reference pins on it, and the ASIC's current on this pin is listed as TBD. With no ASIC boards fitted the regulator certainly runs below its minimum load, and with them it may. The inherited LDO Board A had the same gap.
where: FPGA-LDO A: U8 (bottom side, 93.2, 135.6), net /ASIC_REF_VCM; output capacitors C802 10 uF and C57 1 uF; set resistor R801 7.5k; J3/J4 pin 40.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml: /ASIC_REF_VCM = C57.1, C802.1, J3.40, J4.40, U8.9 (OUTS), U8.10 (OUT); no resistor to AGND. exports/asic/netlist.xml: /REF_VCM = C5, C46, C47, C49 (to /AGND) plus the ASIC LREF_VCM1-4, RREF_VCM1-4 and VCM pins; no resistor. J3_pinout__Power_Pins.csv: REF_VCM 0.75 V, max current 'TBD'. inputs/system/reference_LDO_Board_A/PCB_BOM.csv: R1 7.5k, no load resistor. A 68k load gives 0.75 V / 68 kOhm = 11.0 uA and about 8 uW.
source: ADI LT3042 data sheet Rev A (3042fa), p.4 'Minimum Load Required' row and Note 13 on p.5, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf (read from a third-party copy; analog.com did not answer).
consequence: The common-mode reference shared by all eight ASICs may oscillate or sit noisy or off its set value. Readings taken at bench bring-up without ASIC boards may also mislead.
suggested_action: Add a 68k 0402 resistor from ASIC_REF_VCM to AGND, or get the ASIC designer to confirm that the ASICs always draw at least 10 uA from REF_VCM.

title: One RC starts every ASIC rail with no FPGA control or power-good; the +/-10 V rails need up to about 0.5 s.
what: One resistor-capacitor delay (R1, C3) drives EN_ASIC_RAILS, which enables the LT3582 converter and every regulator; the FPGA cannot switch any rail, and the power-good (PG) outputs that report a rail is in regulation are all left open. Fast start-up is off (PGFB tied to IN), so each rail ramps slowly at a rate set by its SET resistor and capacitor: the 1.5 V LT3042 rails settle about 90 ms after 3.3 V appears and the +/-10 V rails take up to about 0.48 s. The inherited firmware releases CHIP_RESET about 65 ms after FPGA configuration, so it may do so before VDD10/VSS10 are valid. The ASIC reference defines no rail order, so the files cannot say whether this matters; the owner has to decide on firmware delay or hardware control.
where: FPGA-LDO A: R1 (109.4, 140.3), C3 (106.9, 140.3), net /EN_ASIC_RAILS to U1 pin 8 (SHDN), TP4 and the EN pins of U2-U10; PG pin 4 of U2, U6, U8, U9 and U10 unconnected. EN_ASIC_RAILS does not reach J1 or J2. Stimulation power can only be removed by the solder jumpers JP1/JP2.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml: /EN_ASIC_RAILS = C3, R1, TP4, U1.8 and U2-U10 EN; PG pins 'unconnected-'; PGFB = IN on all five LT3042/LT3094. RC timing: R1 10k from VIN_3V3, C3 4.7 uF; Thevenin 10k || 222k (LT3582 SHDN bias) || 125k (four 500k TPS7A20 pull-downs) = 8.9 kOhm, Vinf = 2.93 V, tau = 41.8 ms; 0.9 V reached at 15.3 ms, 1.24 V at 23.0 ms. Soft start, 99% at 4.6 x RSET x CSET: 15k x 1 uF -> 69 ms; 100k x 1 uF -> 460 ms. DC-bias loss on the 25 V 0603 SET capacitors (C903, C1003) probably shortens this to about 0.3-0.45 s (typical X5R behaviour, from memory, not a vendor curve). Schematic note: firmware drives CHIP_RESET high for 2^20 cycles (about 65 ms) at boot. J1 has 13 no-connect pins on both the LDO A and Frontend sides.
source: ADI LT3042 Rev A p.4 (EN/UV threshold) and p.12 (PGFB, fast start-up); ADI LT3094 Rev 0 (start-up time grows with CSET); ADI LT3582 3582512fb (SHDN threshold and current); TI TPS7A20 SBVS338H p.4 and p.7; ASIC_REFERENCE.md open item U02 (no rail sequence).
consequence: The ASICs may leave reset or receive stimulation commands before the +/-10 V rails are valid, and firmware cannot detect it. There is no software way to remove stimulation power in a fault.
suggested_action: At minimum, have firmware wait at least 0.6 s after power-up before releasing CHIP_RESET or enabling stimulation. Better, bring EN_ASIC_RAILS, or a separate enable for U1/U9/U10, to a spare J1 contact driven by the FPGA, which also needs a Frontend change.

title: The DVDD and VDD_ADC regulators return to the opposite ground from the one the ASIC board decouples them to.
what: U5 (DVDD) and its capacitors return to AGND, but the ASIC board decouples DVDD to its digital ground; U3 (VDD_ADC) and its capacitors return to GND, but the ASIC board decouples VDD_ADC to its analog ground. The ASIC board has no tie between its two grounds, so the net tie NT1 (a deliberate single-point copper joint between AGND and GND) is the only bond, and both rails' load current must cross it. The TPS7A20 has no sense pin, so any voltage or noise between AGND and GND appears on the ADC supply. Both arrangements are inherited from LDO Board A; the files cannot show whether the ASIC bonds its grounds inside, and only the ASIC designer can say which ground each rail should reference.
where: FPGA-LDO A: U5 GND pins 2/5, C502.2 and C54.2 on AGND; U3 (110.25, 124.85) GND pins 2/5, C301.2 and C302.2 on GND; NT1 (100.58, 121.0) pin 1 GND, pin 2 AGND; J3/J4 pins 42/44 AGND, 46/48 GND, pin 56 VDD_ADC. ASIC board: placed DVDD capacitors C7, C14 to /DGND (schematic also lists C8-C13); placed VDD_ADC capacitors C1, C34 to /AGND (schematic also lists C35-C38); J3 pins 46/48 = /DGND.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml: U3 GND_2/GND_5 = GND, C301.2/C302.2 = GND; U5 GND_2/GND_5 = AGND, C502.2/C54.2 = AGND; U2/U4/U6/U7/U8/U9/U10 grounds = AGND. exports/asic/pads.csv: only J3, J4 and the two ASICs touch both /AGND and /DGND, so the board has no tie. ASIC_Nine_Rail_Design_Intent.csv: LDO Board A U2 /VDD_ADC referenced to /DGND, U4 /DVDD referenced to /AGND. J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv: DVDD 1.39 mA and VDD_ADC 4.18 mA per board; x4 boards = 5.6 mA and 16.7 mA through NT1.
source: TI TPS7A20 data sheet SBVS338H, Pin Functions p.4 (output capacitor close to the OUT and GND pins of the device), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf; engineering judgement.
consequence: ASIC digital I/O current returns through the analog ground bond, and the ADC supply is referenced to digital ground and shares the single AGND-GND bond. The DC error is negligible; the noise effect is unmeasured.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer which ground each rail should reference. Then move the ground nets of U3 and U5 and their capacitors to match the ASIC board's decoupling.
already_known: Only the VDD_ADC half is recorded: parts_review_V21 START_HERE.md / index.html item S2 (inherited from LDO Board A). The DVDD half is not recorded. Both reviewers agree with minor.

title: Four schematic statements no longer match the board or the Frontend it mates with.
what: Project rules require each circuit block's notes to state its source and changes correctly, and four statements are out of date. The mating note and the J1/J2 description fields name 'Artix Frontend 8L V1', though the mating board is 8L V3, and say the Frontend has not adopted this pin map, though all 140 J1/J2 contacts carry the same nets on both boards. The LT3582 and VIN_3V3 notes refer to current or sag 'at the J1 contacts', but VIN_3V3 enters on J2.68-70. The rail-capacitor note puts C51 and C53-C57 'right at the J3/J4 ports', which holds for C51, C53, C55 and C57 but not for C54 or C56.
where: FPGA-LDO A schematic FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_sch: the Frontend mating, LT3582, VIN_3V3 and rail-capacitor text boxes (among FRONTEND MATING, STIMULATION SUPPLY, VIN_3V3 ENTRY, RAIL CAPACITORS AT THE ASIC PORTS); J1/J2 description fields.
evidence: Text boxes in boards/ldo_a/FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_sch: 'Mate the Artix Frontend 8L V1...'; 'The Frontend has NOT adopted this map yet'; 'start-up current at the J1 contacts'; 'whether VIN_3V3 sags at the J1 contacts'; 'C51 and C53-C57 ... right at the J3/J4 ports'. exports/ldo_a/parts.csv J1/J2 description: 'Artix Frontend 8L V1 ... (Frontend to adopt)'. exports/frontend/connectors.csv vs exports/ldo_a/connectors.csv, J1/J2 pads 1-70: 140/140 equal nets, including 13 no-connects on J1 and 2 on J2. netlist.xml: /VIN_3V3 only on J2.68/69/70. pads.csv distance from capacitor pin 1 to the nearest same-net J3/J4 pin: C51 7.2, C53 7.3, C54 11.4, C55 7.2, C56 (VDD_CGEN) 32.3, C57 7.2 mm.
source: AGENTS.md project rule 'References in schematics' (two explanatory items per block; the source/changes item must be accurate).

suggested_action: Correct the four statements and the J1/J2 description fields in the next schematic revision. No copper change is needed.

title: All 3.3 V input current for the board passes through a single 0.15 mm through via.
what: VIN_3V3 enters on J2.68-70 on the top layer (L1) and reaches the bottom-layer (L6) pour that feeds every regulator through one through via. The only other L1-L6 VIN_3V3 via serves just test point TP1. The expected 167 mA (335 mA in the high case) is well within this via's capacity, and the converter's local input capacitors C1 and C2 sit on L6, so capacity and noise are not the problem. The issue is that there is no second path if this one plated hole is defective, which falls short of the owner's rule that power copper should be thick and thorough.
where: FPGA-LDO A: J2.68/69/70 -> L1 pour L1_PWR_VIN_3V3 (6.3 mm2 piece) -> through via at (109.00, 135.00), 0.15 mm drill, 0.35 mm pad -> L6 pour L6_PWR_VIN_3V3 (113.2 mm2). Other via at (93.725, 140.15) serves TP1 only.
evidence: KiCad pcbnew connectivity on boards/ldo_a/FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_pcb (scratch/verify-ldo_a-batch1, copies of conn.py/conn2.py): VIN_3V3 is one component of 92 nodes; removing via (109.00, 135.00) splits off {J2.68, J2.69, J2.70, the 6.3 and 0.8 mm2 L1 pieces} from the other 83 nodes; removing via (93.72, 140.15) isolates only TP1 and a 22.3 mm2 L1 piece. board.json: VIN_3V3 has two through vias (both 0.15/0.35 mm) and two L5-L6 microvias feeding U1.5 and C1; L1 feed tracks 0.20 mm (J2 pads) and 0.25 mm (to the via); L6 tracks 0.4 mm. Current from system-power result.json: 167 mA expected, 335 mA high on J2.68-70. Via resistance = 1.72e-8 x 1.584e-3 / (pi x 0.17 mm x 0.02 mm), about 2.5 mOhm.
source: Engineering judgement; the owner's rule that power copper should be thick and thorough.
consequence: A single plating void or crack in this via removes power from the whole board.
suggested_action: Add two or three more through vias between the J2 VIN_3V3 pour on L1 and the VIN_3V3 pour on L6.

title: U9, U10 and the TPS7A20 regulators reach ground only through long, shared thin traces; U9's pad has no via.
what: L6 has no ground pour, so U9 (LT3042, VDD10), U10 (LT3094, VSS10) and the TPS7A20 regulators U3/U4/U5 reach their ground plane through daisy-chained 0.10-0.30 mm traces, and U9's exposed pad (the metal pad under the package) has no via. A low-noise regulator sets its output from the voltage on its SET resistor, so any voltage drop between the SET resistor's ground and the plane adds straight onto the output. For U9 that drop path also carries C901's input ripple return and U5's capacitor currents. For U10 the SET resistor's ground leg carries the output capacitors' transient current and U10's own ground current, but not the DC load return of this negative regulator.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12. U9: EP at (95.40,126.34) with no via; chain C902.2 -> 0.30 mm trace to x 90.62 -> 0.15 mm trace along x 90.64 past U5.2/U5.5 and C501.2 -> R901/C903 tap at y 126.81 -> 0.20 mm traces -> via (93.15,130.60) L5-L6 -> buried via (92.90,131.30) L2-L5. U10: C1001.2 -> R1001.2 -> C1003.2 -> C1004.2 -> C1002.2 -> vias (106.45,130.25)/(106.25,131.30). U4.5 returns through the NT1 trace to the J4.42 via. U3 (GND) runs about 10 mm of 0.10-0.20 mm trace to L3 vias (110.78,134.05)/(110.35,134.00).
evidence: conn.py (pcbnew shortest path, in squares of copper) on the V12 board: U9.11 90.7, U9.8 86.5, C901.2 101.5, U5.5 71.1, U4.5 57.2, U10.9 77.8, U3.5 73.3, against 1.0 for the U2/U6/U8 pads. At about 0.49 mOhm per square (35 um copper) the chains are roughly 30-50 mOhm. The U9 segment that matters, R901/C903 tap to plane, is about 37 squares plus two vias, about 20 mOhm. board.json shows no via inside U9's EP; zones.csv shows only power nets on L6, AGND/GND only on L2-L4. The ripple current is not known, so any millivolt figure is an estimate.
source: TI SBVS338H (TPS7A20 data sheet), section 7.4.1 layout guidelines, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf. The LT3042/LT3094 layout guidance on SET and output-capacitor ground was not checked against the datasheet (analog.com could not be reached).
consequence: Ground offsets, possibly at the millivolt level, can appear as ripple and load-dependent shifts on VDD10, VSS10 and the TPS rails, undoing the low-noise benefit of the LT3042/LT3094. No thermal risk at these currents.
suggested_action: Add a laser plus buried via pair to the plane at each regulator's GND/EP pad and at each SET-network ground tap; this respects the V9 instruction against outer-layer ground pours.
already_known: V11_record/START_HERE.md lists 'Row-1 ground returns go through shared drops' as open. The L6 ground pours were removed in V9 at the owner's request ('dont have gnd on top and bottom'). The reviewer agrees it is open; the row-2 and TPS cells are the worst.

title: None of the nine ASIC supply rails has a test point, so bring-up means probing small bottom capacitor pads.
what: The board's test pads TP1-TP9 cover only the input, the +/-12 V stimulation supplies, the enable line, the grounds and the AC input. None sits on the nine ASIC rails (REF_VCM, REF_VDD, VDD_FE, VDD10, VSS10, DVDD, VDD_ADC, VDD_DRIVER, VDD_CGEN). To check them at first power-up, someone has to hold a probe on the regulators' output-capacitor pads on the bottom side; seven of these are small 0402/0603 parts. The ASIC board has no test points either.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12, TP1-TP9. Rail output capacitors, all bottom side: C202, C602, C802 (0603); C502, C302, C402, C702 (0402); C902 (VDD10) and C1002 (VSS10) (1206).
evidence: parts.csv TP1-TP9 nets: VIN_3V3, STIM_POS_12V, STIM_NEG_12V, EN_ASIC_RAILS, GND, AGND, ASIC_AC_IN, STIM_PRE_POS, STIM_PRE_NEG; all 1.0 mm pads, all top except TP8. board.json: every ASIC rail net contains only J3/J4 pins, regulator pins and bottom capacitors and resistors. exports/asic/parts.csv has no TP parts.
source: Engineering judgement (first bring-up of a board that has never been powered or measured).
consequence: A slower and riskier first power-up, with probes that can slip on 0402 pads and short to a neighbouring rail.
suggested_action: Add 0.8-1.0 mm bottom-side test pads on the nine rail pours where there is room, or mark the probe points on the assembly drawing.

title: U3 has no pin-1 mark and the U4/U5 pin-1 dots sit nearer pad 2, so the 1 mm X2SON parts are easy to misorient.
what: U3, U4 and U5 are 1 x 1 mm X2SON regulators (a tiny four-pad leadless package), so pin-1 marks on the silkscreen (the printed ink layer) are the only visual check of their orientation. U3 has no pin-1 mark, and the dots for U4 and U5 sit closer to pad 2 than to pad 1, which can mislead an inspector. Almost no reference designators are printed: only board-text labels for J1-J4, U7 and NT1, so all bottom parts appear only on the assembly drawing. The board title block is empty, but the board name and V12 are carried by the file names, the Gerber header and the silkscreen, so that part is cosmetic.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12, bottom side. U3 pin 1 at (109.925,124.42), no dot nearby. U4 dot at (99.22,124.42): pin 1 at x 97.825, pin 2 at x 98.475. U5 dot at (91.11,124.22): pin 1 at x 89.625, pin 2 at x 90.275. Board setup title block.
evidence: pcbnew script (silk2.py): 0 of 84 reference fields visible on silk; bottom silk texts PRE+, U7, J4 ASIC, NT1; 8 bottom pin-1 circles (U7, U5, U8, U2, U6, U4, U9, U10), none near U3. CPL rotation for U3/U4/U5 is -90. summary.txt: title, rev and date empty. V12_order/FPGA_LDO_A_V12_gerbers.zip header: %TF.ProjectId,FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12,...,rev?*%; top silk includes 'FPGA-LDO A V12' and '2026-11-10'.
source: Engineering judgement; JLC's assembly placement review step.
consequence: A rotated X2SON regulator can pass visual inspection and be found only at power-up, because U3-U5 orientation rests on placement-file rotations that have not been checked against JLC's part images.
suggested_action: Confirm U3/U4/U5 pin 1 (and the U1-U10 rotations) in JLC's placement preview, and move the U4/U5 dots to the pad-1 corner if the silkscreen is touched; optionally fill in the title block.
already_known: V12_record/START_HERE.md (silkscreen limits; placement rotations unchecked).

title: Nobody has checked that U10's output capacitors keep the LT3094's 10 uF minimum after DC-bias derating.
what: The LT3094 needs at least 10 uF of ceramic output capacitance to stay stable. U10's output has 32 uF nominal (22 uF 1206 plus 10 uF 0805, both 25 V X5R) at -10 V. Ceramic capacitors lose much of their value under DC voltage (DC-bias derating), heat and tolerance, the small 0805 most of all, and Samsung's product pages give no DC-bias data. The same unchecked question applies to C902 at U9 (LT3042, 4.7 uF minimum, more margin) and to the +/-12 V converter outputs, which sit at 12 V and are likely to lose the largest fraction.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12. ASIC_VSS10 (-10 V, R1001 100k): C1002 (CL31A226KAHNNNE) and C1004 (CL21A106KAYNNNE) at U10.10-12. ASIC_VDD10: C902 (CL31A226KAHNNNE) at U9. STIM_POS_12V / STIM_NEG_12V: C14 and C21 (CL21A226MAYNNNE, 22 uF 0805), plus C901/C1001 (10 uF 0805) on STIM_PRE_POS/NEG through the bridged JP1/JP2.
evidence: board.json nets: /ASIC_VSS10 = C1002.1, C1004.1, J3.54, J4.54, U10.10-12; /ASIC_VDD10 = C902.1, J3/J4.36, U9.9/10. parts.csv MPNs as listed. Samsung product pages for CL21A106KAYNNN and CL31A226KAHNNN: 25 V, X5R, +/-10 %, no DC-bias curve. A rough estimate from typical X5R behaviour (from memory, not a datasheet) leaves about 15-18 uF at 10 V, so failure is unlikely but not proven.
source: ADI LT3094 data sheet Rev B, output capacitor section (10 uF ceramic minimum confirmed from ADI's product page, https://www.analog.com/en/products/lt3094.html); LT3042 Rev B (4.7 uF minimum). The data sheet PDFs could not be opened, so the ESR limit and page numbers were not checked against the datasheet.
consequence: If the effective capacitance at -10 V and temperature falls below 10 uF, the -10 V ASIC rail can ring or oscillate.
suggested_action: Read Samsung's DC-bias curves for these parts at 10 V and 12 V (or measure them); if the -10 V total falls below about 13 uF at 25 C, make C1004 a second 22 uF 1206.
already_known: parts_review_V21/START_HERE.md S6 (+/-12 V caps).

title: D11 and D12 (B0540WS-7) are out of stock at JLC, and the proposed B5819WS substitute is unchecked.
what: The two Schottky diodes of the LT3582 boost and inverting converter showed 0 in stock at JLC, and the LT3582 data sheet names the B0540WS for this job. The 5 Nov cart's substitute, B5819WS, has not been checked against the circuit's limits. A substitute needs a 40 V-class reverse rating, a peak current rating above the inverting switch limit of 720 mA, an average rating only above the small output load, low leakage when hot, and the same SOD-323 pad.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12, bottom side, SOD-323. D11: anode /SW_P (U1 pin 12, L11), cathode /CAPP (U1 pins 10/11, C15). D12: cathode /SW_N (U1 pins 3/4, L12), anode /STIM_NEG_12V (U1 pin 2).
evidence: inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/parts_status.csv row C98664: stock 0, orderable -173 (read 10 Nov 2026, 16:04). Reverse voltage about 15.3 V on D12 and about 12.3-12.8 V on D11 (netlist.xml topology). LT3582 Rev B p.4: inverting switch limit 490/600/720 mA, boost 285/350/430 mA, output disconnect 124/155/186 mA. Schematic note: inductor peaks 0.42/0.69 A. pads.csv: 0.60 x 0.45 mm pads at 2.10 mm centres (2.70 mm overall). LCSC C98664: 40 V, 500 mA, 5 uA at 30 V.
source: ADI LT3582 data sheet Rev B (3582512fb), p.4 electrical characteristics, p.19 'Diode Selection', Fig. 13 p.22, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf (read from a local copy). Diodes DS30524 could not be opened.
consequence: The board cannot be assembled until a diode is sourced. A leaky substitute lowers efficiency when warm.
suggested_action: Order B0540WS-7 through JLC Global Sourcing, or check B5819WS (or another part) against the limits above before putting it in the BOM.
already_known: V12_record/START_HERE.md; the reviewer agrees.

title: CPL rotations are unchecked against JLC, and a 180-degree DF40 placement error would put 3.3 V on signal pins.
what: The CPL (the placement file that tells JLC where and at what angle to place each part) copies KiCad's rotation and side for all 72 parts with no per-package correction. JLC's library parts often use a different zero angle, and nobody has compared the rotations with JLC's part images. The Hirose DF40 connectors have no polarity key, so a 180-degree placement error on J1-J4 would not be caught when the boards are mated. On J2 that error would put VIN_3V3 onto ASIC signal lines.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12 CPL: J1, J2 (top, -90), J3 (top, 0), J4 (bottom, 0), U1-U10, D11, D12. J2 pins 68-70 (VIN_3V3) swap with pins 3/2/1 (ASIC5_SYNC, ASIC5_READ, STIM_CHB_SHARED); J3/J4 pin 1 (ASIC_VDD_CGEN) swaps with pin 80 (ASIC7_DATA1 / ASIC3_DATA1).
evidence: inputs/ldo_a/V12_scripts/make_jlc_v12.py sets rotation = float(r['Rot']) from pos_kicad.csv with no offset table. inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/FPGA_LDO_A_V12_CPL_JLC.csv against exports/ldo_a/parts.csv: 72 rows, 0 differences in rotation or side. exports/ldo_a/pads.csv with pin n mapped to 71-n (DF40 70-pin) or 81-n (80-pin) gives the swaps listed. JLC part models could not be read.
source: JLC 'Confirm Parts Placement' review step; Hirose DF40 catalog (no polarity), read from distributor copies, not hirose.com; engineering judgement.
consequence: A rotated IC, diode or connector on the first boards, found only at power-up; on a DF40 it can put supply voltage on signal pins.
suggested_action: In JLC's placement review, check pin 1 of J1-J4 and U1-U10 and the D11/D12 cathodes against the assembly drawings before confirming the order.
already_known: V12_record/START_HERE.md 'Before ordering'. The reviewer agrees; the connector risk is not stated there.

title: 29 of 72 placed parts have no MPN, so the order BOM's JLC part choices exist only in a script table.
what: An MPN (manufacturer part number) and an LCSC number (JLC's stock code) in each symbol tell anyone building a BOM exactly which part to buy. On this schematic 29 of the 72 placed parts have no MPN and only five carry an LCSC number. The order BOM instead picks each JLC part from a value-and-footprint table inside make_jlc_v12.py. A BOM regenerated from the schematic alone would lose the JLC numbers and the passive part choices, though it would keep the 43 MPNs that are present (every IC, connector, diode and the 0805/1206 capacitors).
where: FPGA-LDO Option A, schematic V30A. No MPN: C1, C2, C11, C16, C17, C51, C53-C57, C203, C603, C803, R1-R6, R16-R19, R201, R601, R801, R901, R1001. LCSC field only on U2, U6, U8, U9 (C580010) and U10 (C670492). L11/L12 MPN field DFE201610E-6R8M=P2.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/parts.csv: 84 footprints, 72 placed after excluding TP/JP/NT; MPN empty for the 29 refs above. C1 Voltage field 10V, C2 16V. inputs/ldo_a/V12_scripts/make_jlc_v12.py: docstring says the JLC numbers are not in schematic V30; its table maps ('22uF','C_0805') to CL21A226MAYNNNE (25 V) and ('100nF','C_0402') to CL05B104KB54PNC (50 V), so both voltage fields understate the ordered parts. inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/parts_status.csv: L11/L12 'no part chosen'. Neither the project record nor the re-check found a listing for DFE201610E-6R8M=P2; Murata's own database page did not load, so its existence is unproven either way.
source: Engineering judgement (good practice). The workspace rule requires populated Datasheet properties and on-page citations, not MPN or LCSC fields.
consequence: A later BOM, or reuse of this schematic for Option B, could order different passives than the ones chosen for V12 without anyone noticing. The C1/C2 voltage mismatches point to a higher rating on the ordered part, so they carry no electrical risk.
suggested_action: Copy the MPN and LCSC numbers from the JLC BOM into the symbol fields, correct the C1/C2 voltage fields, and confirm or replace the L11/L12 MPN.
already_known: V12_record/START_HERE.md mentions it in passing; not raised as an issue.

title: U1 has no fixed frequency, so its ripple can alias into the recording band as a tone that moves with load.
what: U1 (LT3582-12) has no fixed-frequency or sync mode: its frequency sits near 48-52 kHz at light load and rises with load. Each ASIC channel is sampled at 31.25 kS/s, so ripple that reaches a sampled node shows up 'aliased' (folded) at |f - n x 31.25 kHz|, somewhere between 0 and 15.6 kHz, and that tone moves when the ±12 V load changes. Folding itself is not new: the replaced TPS65130 (1.25-1.50 MHz) and the Frontend's MPM3833C that makes VIN_3V3 (about 1.15 MHz) also alias into the band; what U1 adds is a load-dependent tone. The ripple level that reaches the ASIC is not known and has not been worked out, so only a bring-up measurement can settle whether it matters.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A, U1 LT3582EUD-12 (bottom, pin 12 SW_P, pins 3/4 SW_N, pin 5 VIN on VIN_3V3). U1 feeds only U9 LT3042 (ASIC_VDD10, via STIM_POS_12V, JP1, STIM_PRE_POS) and U10 LT3094 (ASIC_VSS10, via STIM_NEG_12V, JP2, STIM_PRE_NEG). The other seven LDOs (U2-U8) see U1 only through its input-current pulses on VIN_3V3 and through GND/AGND (NT1). Bench option: TP8/TP9, TP6 AGND.
evidence: LT3582 data sheet p.6 G01, digitised (VIN 5 V, Figure 13 circuit with 6.8 uH as on this board): both outputs about 48-52 kHz from 0 to 2 mA; boost/inverter about 147/98 kHz at 5 mA, 280/177 kHz at 10 mA, 641/368 kHz at 25 mA. p.7 G10/G13: single pulses about 20 us apart at 1 mA. Scaling the boost to VIN 3.3 V by the DCM energy ratio (12.5/7.5 vs 12.5/9.2, factor 1.227) gives about 183/346/785 kHz; the inverter does not change with VIN. Loads: LT3042 quiescent about 2 mA, LT3094 about 2.35 mA; the ASIC designer's budget (J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv) gives 2 mA each on VDD10/VSS10 per board, about 10 mA per output for four boards; 8 ASICs x 128 x 22.5 uA = 23 mA with all stimulators on. Folded tones: 52 -> 10.5, 61-64 -> 1.5, 99 -> 5.25, 182 -> 5.5, 178 -> 9.5, 345 -> 1.25, 367 -> 8.0, 782 -> 0.75 kHz. TPS65130 1.25-1.50 MHz spans 40-48 x 31.25 kHz; MPM3833C 1.15 MHz folds to about 6.25 kHz. LT3042/LT3094 PSRR at 1 MHz 79/74 dB (front pages). Schematic V30A LT3582 note lists 'ripple after layout' as unverified; parts review V21 still gives the TPS65130 fixed-frequency rationale.
source: ADI LT3582/LT3582-5/LT3582-12 data sheet 3582512fb, Rev B: p.6 G01, p.7 G10-G14, p.10 Operation, p.19, p.22 Figure 13, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf; TI TPS65130 SLVS493E p.6 (fS); MPS MPM3833C product page (forced CCM frequency); inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md B6 (0.3-10 kHz), B12 (31.25 kS/s), B16 (22.5 uA), B18 (stimulation under 200 Hz), 6.5 uVrms integrated noise.
consequence: If enough ripple survives the ASIC's supply rejection (no ASIC specification gives it), recordings could show narrow tones in the 0.3-10 kHz band whose frequency depends on the unit and the static stimulator load. A bad result costs a jumper cut and a bench supply, not a board spin.
suggested_action: At bring-up, record ASIC shorted-input spectra with U1 running and with JP1/JP2 cut and bench ±12 V on TP8/TP9, at idle and with dummy loads, and look for tones at |f_sw - n x 31.25 kHz| against the 6.5 uVrms noise figure.

title: The order sets no bottom stencil thickness; above 0.10 mm the X2SON pin apertures release paste poorly.
what: Solder paste leaves a stencil hole cleanly only if the hole's open area is large compared with its wall area; this 'area ratio' is usually kept at 0.66 or more (IPC-7525 guideline). The X2SON pin apertures of the four TPS7A2015 regulators copy TI's own example stencil, which TI bases on a 0.075-0.1 mm stencil, giving 0.61 at 0.10 mm, 0.51 at 0.12 mm and 0.41 at 0.15 mm. The assembly remark does not name a stencil thickness, and JLC publishes no default for its assembly service; because the bottom side also carries the 0.4 mm pitch J4, 0.10-0.12 mm is the likely choice and 0.15 mm unlikely. Separately, the exposed-pad (EP, the centre thermal pad) paste is a 45-degree rounded square with 24 % more paste than TI's round aperture.
evidence: B_Paste.gbp in FPGA_LDO_A_V12_gerbers.zip and footprint Texas_X2SON-4_1x1mm_P0.65mm.kicad_mod: pin aperture 0.40 x 0.21 mm with 0.18 mm chamfer, area 0.0678 mm2, perimeter 1.115 mm. Area ratio A/(P x t) = 0.61 / 0.51 / 0.41 at t = 0.10 / 0.12 / 0.15 mm. J4 (0.4 mm DF40, bottom): 0.80 / 0.67 / 0.54 at the same thicknesses; DFN and QFN pins about 0.83-0.84 at 0.12 mm. EP paste 0.197 mm2 against 0.159 mm2 for TI's 0.45 mm round; EP-to-pin paste ratio 2.9 against TI's 2.35. inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/JLC_Remarks_paste.txt names no stencil thickness.
source: TI TPS7A20 data sheet SBVS338H, DQN0004A Example Stencil Design (4215302/E): 4X 0.21 x 0.4 mm pins, 0.45 mm round EP, 88 % coverage, based on 0.075-0.1 mm stencil, note 9 (IPC-7525), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf. JLC stencil guide (0.4 mm pitch common 0.10 mm, 0.5 mm 0.12 mm, 0.65 mm 0.15 mm), https://jlcpcb.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-solder-paste-stencil; JLC stencil and PCBA capability pages (no PCBA default stated).
consequence: If JLC picks 0.12 mm or more, paste release on the four 1 x 1 mm regulators varies from print to print, which can leave weak or open pin joints on four of the nine ASIC rails. Repair is hot-air rework of 1 x 1 mm bottom-side parts, not a board spin.
suggested_action: Add 'bottom stencil 0.10 mm, laser-cut, electropolished' (or a step-down at U3/U4/U5/U7) to the assembly remark and ask JLC to confirm the stencil thickness it will use.

title: Nothing discharges the ±10 V ASIC rails, so they can stay charged for seconds after the 1.5 V rails fall.
what: When VIN_3V3 goes away, the 1.5 V regulators lose their input and their outputs fall with it. ASIC_VDD10 and ASIC_VSS10 have no bleed resistor and drain only through the ASIC and regulator leakage, so with little ASIC current they stay near ±10 V for hundreds of milliseconds to seconds. The built-in discharge features do not help: the TPS7A2015 pulldown acts only while EN is low and input is still present, and the LT3582 discharge acts only on its own ±12 V outputs, not on the LT3042/LT3094 outputs. No ASIC power-down requirement exists, so the files cannot say whether the ASIC tolerates live stimulator rails over an unpowered core; only the ASIC designer can.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A: ASIC_VDD10 (U9 LT3042 OUT, C902 22 uF, J3/J4 pin 36) and ASIC_VSS10 (U10 LT3094 OUT, C1002 22 uF + C1004 10 uF, J3/J4 pin 54). 1.5 V rails from U3/U4/U5/U7 TPS7A2015PDQNR and U2/U6/U8 LT3042, all fed from VIN_3V3. EN_ASIC_RAILS from R1 10k / C3 4.7 uF.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/nets.csv: /ASIC_VDD10 = C902.1, J3.36, J4.36, U9.9/10 only; /ASIC_VSS10 = C1002.1, C1004.1, J3.54, J4.54, U10.10-12 only, so no bleed path. /EN_ASIC_RAILS drives U1 SHDN and U2-U10 EN; R1 10k, C3 4.7 uF (47 ms), reaching 0.3 V about 106 ms after VIN_3V3 collapses. TPS7A20 SBVS338H: 150 ohm output pulldown only when VEN < VEN(LOW) = 0.3 V (spec at VIN 3.1 V). LT3582 3582512fb: VIN minimum 2.4-2.55 V (p.2); output discharge permanently enabled on the -12 version and acts on SHDN falling (p.10, p.16). Prior shutdown model (shutdown2_out.txt) at 0 mA ASIC load: VDD10 still 10.00 V at 0.8 s (idealised, no leakage), VSS10 to about -9.45 / -8.19 V through the LT3094 OUT-to-IN path. ASIC_REFERENCE.md sections 4, 7 and 10 give no rail sequence or window.
source: TI TPS7A20 data sheet SBVS338H, p.3 EN pin and p.7 electrical characteristics, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf; ADI LT3582 data sheet 3582512fb Rev B, p.2, p.10, p.16, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf. No ASIC power-down requirement exists; otherwise engineering judgement.
consequence: If the ASIC needs its ±10 V rails to fall before or with its 1.5 V rails, every unplug or host shutdown leaves the stimulator supply live over an unpowered core, with undefined stimulator state. If it does not, there is no effect.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer whether VDD10/VSS10 may stay live while the 1.5 V rails are off; if not, add a bleed resistor from each ±10 V rail to AGND (for example 10-22 kOhm, about 5-10 mW).
already_known: system-power.json and system-bringup.json note that no ASIC power-up order is known; neither covers power-down. Reviewer agrees with minor.

title: Many L1 lanes run directly over other nets' L2 lanes, and L5 lanes sit closer to L6 rail pours than to L4 GND.
what: L1-L2 and L5-L6 are only 0.071 mm apart, while L4-L5 is 0.201 mm. Where one trace runs directly over another net's trace on the next layer ('broadside' coupling), the two couple strongly, and an L5 trace over an L6 rail pour returns its current partly through that rail rather than through GND. L2, named the AGND plane, carries 466 mm of signal tracks, which is why L1 lanes sit over L2 lanes. The amounts are modest at these lengths, but no signal-integrity check has been made.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12. L1 over L2, for example ASIC8_SYNC over ASIC6_SYNC for 11.5 mm and ASIC8_DATA1 over ASIC6_DATA2 for 9.7 mm. L5 (In4) lanes over L6 (B.Cu) pours: ASIC_DVDD 58 mm, ASIC_VSS10 47 mm, ASIC_VDD_ADC 43.5 mm, ASIC_VDD10 23 mm, plus VIN_3V3 93 mm and STIM_PRE_POS/NEG 80 mm.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/stackup.txt: dielectric 1 = 0.071 mm (1078), dielectric 4 = 0.201 mm (7628), dielectric 5 = 0.071 mm. exports/ldo_a/board.json: track length L1 717.5, L2 465.9, L5 1000.7, L6 718.5 mm; stacked lanes 0.1 mm wide. Overlap of other-net copper sampled every 0.02 mm: 222 mm of L1 signal over L2 signal across 203 net pairs. pcbnew on filled B.Cu pours: 184 mm of L5 lanes over ASIC-rail pours (DVDD 58.4, VSS10 47.0, VDD_ADC 43.5, VDD10 23.1, VDD_DRIVER 5.9, REF_VDD 5.7, VDD_CGEN 0.4 mm), VIN_3V3 93.4, STIM_PRE_POS 41.4, STIM_PRE_NEG 38.4 mm. Parallel-plate estimate about 0.6 pF over 11.5 mm before fringing; with about 70 ps electrical length against a 1 ns edge, backward crosstalk on a 1.5 V swing is some tens of mV.
source: Engineering judgement.
consequence: Some crosstalk between neighbouring ASIC data and SYNC lanes and some digital noise coupled onto the ASIC rails, likely within LVCMOS15 margins.
suggested_action: No change needed now; include the stacked lane pairs and the L5-over-rail runs in any signal-integrity check of the Frontend-LDO-ASIC path.

title: The boost switch node SW_P sits about 2 mm from the REF_VCM regulator's SET trace and REF_VCM pour on L6.
what: SW_P is the boost converter's switch node, a square wave of about 0 to 12.5 V. On L6 it runs just south of U8, the LT3042 that makes the ASIC's common-mode reference REF_VCM. Coupling into the SET pin should be small, because C803 (1 uF) shunts SET to AGND and the nearby AGND pad is tied to the plane. This is a watch item for the first noise measurement, not a defect.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12, L6 (bottom): SW_P (U1 pin 12, L11 pad 2 at about x 95.17, y 140.55, D11 anode). C802 pad 2 (AGND), U8 SET trace (0.15 mm wide at y 137.7, x 93.7-96.555), L6_PWR_ASIC_REF_VCM pour.
evidence: Exact copper-shape distances from the board with pcbnew (roundrect pads, ratio 0.25): L11.2 to C802.2 (AGND) 1.144 mm; to the Net-(U8-SET) track 1.975 mm; to the L6 ASIC_REF_VCM pour 2.004 mm, the closest REF_VCM copper. exports/ldo_a/board.json: SW_P has pads and tracks only on L6, no vias. C803 1 uF on Net-(U8-SET)/AGND. The LT3582 frequency varies with load (data sheet p.10), so any spur frequency also moves.
source: Engineering judgement.
consequence: Possible small switching spur on REF_VCM, the ASIC's common-mode reference.
suggested_action: On the first board, measure REF_VCM noise around the LT3582 switching frequency at idle and under load.
already_known: V11_record/START_HERE.md: 'row-2 output caps face the converter. Not measured or simulated.'

title: The board's minimum solder-mask web is 0, so DRC would not catch a thin mask sliver added by a later edit.
what: Solder mask is the coating between pads; the thin strip of mask left between two pad openings is called the mask web or dam. KiCad only checks these strips against the board's minimum web setting, and on this board that setting is 0, so DRC reports only openings that actually touch. The custom rule file covers via rings, hole clearance, edge clearance and silkscreen, not mask webs. Today the smallest real web is about 0.17 mm, above JLC's 0.10 mm green limit, so nothing is wrong now.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_pcb setup block (no solder_mask_min_width, so it defaults to 0; pad_to_mask_clearance 0); FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_dru. Smallest webs at J1 DF40 pads and at the X2SON U3/U4/U5/U7 pin openings next to the exposed-pad opening.
evidence: Board file: pcbnew reports m_SolderMaskMinWidth 0.0. Scratch DRC (KiCad 10.0.6): web 0.10 mm or 0.13 mm gives no new violations; 0.18 mm gives 199 solder_mask_bridge errors (DF40 pads), which shows the check works once set. Mask-web scan: smallest 0.170 mm (J1 DF40 pads; X2SON pin openings to EP opening, mask margin -0.05 mm). The V12 record's 0.12 mm figure is the X2SON copper pad-to-pad gap, not the mask web. The .kicad_pro sets lib_footprint_mismatch, lib_footprint_issues, track_not_centered_on_via, missing_courtyard, footprint_filters_mismatch and footprint_type_mismatch to ignore; turned to warnings they give 53 lib_footprint_mismatch + 12 track_not_centered_on_via and nothing else (library comparison: pad positions and sizes equal the library for every footprint type).
source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities, solder mask bridge 0.10 mm green / 0.13 mm black and white (1 oz), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities; KiCad DRC solder_mask_bridge behaviour.
consequence: No effect on the current files; JLC's CAM also handles its own mask bridges. A sliver added by a later edit would pass DRC unreported.
suggested_action: Set the board's minimum mask web to 0.10 mm (JLC green) and re-run DRC; it is clean today at that value.

title: JLC holds only 55 TPS7A2015PDQNR for the 20 needed, a cart does not reserve them, and TI has none in stock.
what: Each board uses four TPS7A2015PDQNR LDOs (low-dropout regulators) in the tiny X2SON package, so five boards need 20. JLC listed 55 when the order file was made. Adding parts to a cart does not hold stock, so other buyers could take them first, and TI itself lists the part as out of stock (samples only), so a refill would not be quick.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12: U3, U4, U5, U7 (TPS7A2015PDQNR, JLC/LCSC C2862700, extended part).
evidence: inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/parts_status.csv row C2862700: 4 per board, need 20, JLC stock 55, orderable 55, read 10 Nov 2026 16:04. FPGA_LDO_A_V12_BOM_JLC.csv and exports/ldo_a/bom.csv: U3-U5, U7 = TPS7A2015PDQNR, quantity 4. ti.com part page: Active, X2SON DQN 4-pin, 3000-unit reel, TI stock out of stock / samples only. Today's JLC and LCSC stock could not be read (pages load stock by script).
source: JLC part page C2862700, https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C2862700; TI TPS7A20 data sheet SBVS338H orderable information (Active); TI TPS7A2015PDQNR part page on ti.com.
consequence: If the stock is gone at order time the boards wait, or the 1.5 V rails need a substitute LDO with a different footprint.
suggested_action: Secure the 20 parts (pre-order or reserve) at the same time as the U1 order, and re-read JLC stock just before ordering.
