title: The LT3094 rejects little of the inverter's fast edges near 10 MHz, so VSS10 edge noise is unbounded on paper.
what: The LT3582 converter makes the +/-12 V supplies by switching, which leaves ripple at its switching frequency plus fast nanosecond edges, mostly on the -12 V side. The LT3094 that makes VSS10 has a PSRR (power-supply rejection ratio: how much input noise it keeps off its output) of about 80 dB near 1 MHz but only about 25-35 dB at 10 MHz, and its data sheet gives nothing higher. The LT3042 that makes VDD10 still gives about 57-80 dB at 10 MHz, so VDD10 is less exposed. How much edge noise reaches VSS10 depends on layout and output capacitors and must be measured.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12: D12 / C21 / JP2 / C1001 -> U10 (LT3094, VSS10, output caps C1002, C1004); D11 / C15 / C14 / JP1 / C901 -> U9 (LT3042, VDD10, output cap C902); both rails reach the ASIC boards through J4.
evidence: LT3094 Rev 0 p.11 G45 and p.12 G46 at IL = -1 mA: about 85 dB near 100 kHz, 78-80 dB at 1 MHz, peak near 2 MHz, about 25-35 dB at 10 MHz. LT3042 Rev A p.10 G43 at 1 mA: about 84 dB at 1 MHz, 76-80 dB at 10 MHz; p.9 G41/G42: about 57-65 dB at 10 MHz at 50-200 mA. The review's ripple model (outside.py, not re-run by the checker): VOUTN 1.6 / 4.3 / 6.4 mV rms and VOUTP 0.5-0.8 mV rms at 2 / 10 / 25 mA, edge spikes on VOUTN about 0.1 V p-p, sensitive to assumed capacitor ESL. nets.csv gives the regulator and output-capacitor nets.
source: ADI LT3094 data sheet Rev 0, p.11-12 (G45-G47), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3094.pdf; ADI LT3042 data sheet Rev A, p.9-10 (G41-G43), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3042fb.pdf; LT3582 data sheet p.22 (output ripple reference).
consequence: Probably harmless for stimulation, but VSS10 also feeds the ASIC and shares its AGND, so unmeasured high-frequency content is a possible path for noise into recordings.
suggested_action: Add VSS10 and VDD10 at the J4 pins to the bring-up ripple measurement, using a 20 MHz-bandwidth probe with a short ground spring.

title: A -12 V trace passes 0.10 mm from U1's GND pin 1, the tightest pad-to-track gap on the board.
what: On the bottom layer, the /STIM_NEG_12V trace runs beside U1 pin 1, which is a GND pad with its mask opening exactly at the copper edge. The gap between the open pad and the -12 V copper is 0.100 mm. This meets JLC's 0.09 mm rule for mask opening to trace and exactly meets JLC's and the board's own 0.10 mm pad-to-track minimum, so it is not a rule violation. It is the smallest pad-to-other-net-track gap on the board, and a short here would join -12 V to ground.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12, L6 (bottom): U1 pad 1 (GND), copper and mask opening right edge x = 101.875, y 141.725-141.975; /STIM_NEG_12V track, 0.25 mm wide, x = 102.1, y 141.40-142.35 (left edge 101.975).
evidence: board.json: U1 pad 1 bbox [101.0, 141.725, 101.875, 141.975], net GND; track {/STIM_NEG_12V, w 0.25, (102.1, 142.35)-(102.1, 141.4)}; 101.975 - 101.875 = 0.100 mm. B_Mask.gbs: U1 pad 1 flash D45 RoundRect 0.875 x 0.25 mm, mask expansion 0 (pad_to_mask_clearance 0). L6 .gbl: D56 = C 0.25 at x 102.1. Scan of all mask-open pads: U1-1 0.100 mm, C901-2 0.11 mm, many J3/J4 0.4 mm pitch pads 0.112 mm, others 0.125 mm or more.
source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities, solder mask opening to trace 0.09 mm minimum and pad to track (1 oz) 0.1 mm minimum, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities
consequence: Builds as drawn within JLC's limits. A solder bridge at this spot would short the -12 V stimulation supply to ground at power-up.
suggested_action: Optionally move the 0.25 mm segment at x = 102.1 about 0.05 mm east so the gap is about 0.15 mm.

title: The V12 record's 0.12 mm smallest mask bridge is the copper gap; the real smallest mask dam is 0.17 mm.
what: A mask dam is the strip of solder mask left between two neighbouring pad openings. Measured directly from both mask Gerbers, no dam on the board is below JLC's 0.10 mm limit: the smallest is 0.200 mm on the bottom and 0.170 mm on the top. The only merged openings are the bridged jumpers JP1 and JP2, which are meant to be one opening. The V12 record gives 0.12 mm (X2SON) as the smallest mask bridge, but that is the copper pad-to-pad gap; the X2SON mask openings sit 0.05 mm inside the copper, so the real X2SON dam is 0.2196 mm.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12: B_Mask.gbs (0.200 mm at J4 0.4 mm pitch pads and between U2/U6/U8 DFN pins and their exposed pads); F_Mask.gts (0.170 mm at J1, J2 and J3, 0.23 mm pads at 0.4 mm pitch); X2SON U3/U4/U5/U7 pin to EP 0.2196 mm; JP1 (90.15, 136.2), JP2 (109.75, 142.5).
evidence: Openings rebuilt from the Gerbers (flashes, RoundRect and FreePoly macros, regions) with every pairwise gap computed: bottom 295 openings (293 flashes + 2 regions), minimum 0.200 mm, 4 overlaps only at JP1/JP2, 0 dams under 0.10 mm; top 242 openings, minimum 0.170 mm. Board file: solder_mask_margin -0.05 on the X2SON footprints; board.json setup mask_min_width 0.0. V12_record/START_HERE.md line 37: solder mask bridge 0.12 mm smallest (X2SON).
source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities, soldermask bridge 0.10 mm (green, 1 oz), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities
consequence: No effect on this order. The minimum-web-0 setting matters only for later edits, because DRC still would not catch a new sliver.
suggested_action: Correct the record's 0.12 mm figure to 0.17 mm (mask dam), and set the board's minimum mask web to 0.10 mm so later edits are checked.
already_known: The rule-set item (minimum mask web 0) is already reported; this corrects its practical impact.

title: Bottom IC pad vias all sit under paste, and their needed filled-and-capped finish is only in the order remark.
what: Several vias sit inside soldered pads (via-in-pad), and on the bottom ICs every one lies fully under a paste window, where solder paste is printed. Such vias must be filled with epoxy and capped with copper, or solder drains into the hole. The order remark asks JLC for epoxy filled and capped vias with copper-filled laser vias, and JLC applies this by default to 6+ layer boards; the 0.15 mm through holes are inside JLC's 0.15-0.55 mm range, but the KiCad board file records only tenting, not filling or capping.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12, bottom side: through vias in the exposed pads of U1 (LT3582) at (100.36, 142.24) and (100.36, 142.96), U2 at (98.3, 135.3), U6 at (103.95, 135.3) and (105.05, 135.3), U8 at (92.65, 135.3) and (93.75, 135.3); laser vias in pin 3 of U2/U6/U8 at (98.85 / 104.5 / 93.2, 134.15). The X2SON parts U3/U4/U5/U7 have no vias in their pads.
evidence: vip.py on board.json and the L1/L6 and paste Gerbers: via ends inside SMD pads, laser 78 on L1 + 33 on L6 = 111, through 24 on L1 + 52 on L6 = 76, matching the remark. Via types: 100 L1-L2 laser, 85 L5-L6 laser, 68 buried, 64 through 0.15 mm hole / 0.35 mm pad. Example: U2 paste [97.775-98.735, 134.855-135.525] contains barrel 98.125-98.475. Only exposed via ends without paste: TP5, TP6 (top) and JP2 pad 2 (bottom). Board file setup lines 126-139: tenting front/back yes; covering, plugging, filling, capping no.
source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities, Epoxy Filled & Capped, via diameters 0.15-0.55 mm, default for 6 layers and above, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities; Engineering judgement (general via-in-pad practice).
consequence: If the filled-and-capped option or the remark were dropped on a re-order or with another factory, solder would wick into the exposed-pad vias and the pads could end up with voids or too little solder.
suggested_action: Keep the filled-and-capped option and the via-in-pad remark on every order, and note the requirement in the board's fabrication notes.
already_known: JLC_Remarks_paste.txt states the counts and the filled-and-capped choice.
